description: Building an interactive 3D CubeSat Mission Control game powered by React, Three.js, real-time SGP4 orbital physics, and Gemini AI. Players engineer a 1U spacecraft under strict mass, power, and budget trade-offs, deploy into Low Earth Orbit, and manage live thermal and telemetry constraints to complete mission objectives. Focused on shipping a high-FPS aerospace sim!
summary:
Nadir Dynamics: Space Mission Design Lab is an interactive 3D space mission engineering game that transforms abstract orbital, RF, thermal, and mass-budget trade-offs into hands-on gameplay for Beginner/Youth learners and experienced enthusiasts.
Starting from a bare Cal Poly CDS Rev 13 aluminum CubeSat frame, players assemble 1U/3U/6U spacecraft piece-by-piece across 6 subsystems and 5 scientific instruments, select launch vehicles and SGP4 orbits, balance 6 competing resources (Mass, Eclipse Power, Cost, Flash Storage, RF Link Margin, Orbital Lifetime), and pilot live orbital passes around a photorealistic 3D Earth with a real solar day/night terminator.
Using real-time Meteomatics atmospheric cloud cover and rain-fade data (with deterministic climatological fallback), players experience why West African flood monitoring favors all-weather SAR radar over optical cameras—supporting solo play, 4-role co-op crews, competitive team races, a Space Systems Field Guide, and a Gemini AI Flight Director.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Nadir Dynamics models the complete CubeSat mission lifecycle across 5 phases: Mission Briefing, Bare-Frame 3D Assembly, Orbit & Launch Gate Validation, Live Orbital Flight Operations, and Root-Cause Post-Mission Debrief.

• Piece-by-Piece 3D CAD Assembly: Players mount subsystems (Solar, Battery/EPS, ADCS Reaction Wheels/Star Tracker, OBC, Thermal Louvers/MLI, UHF/S/X-Band Comms) and scientific payloads (Optical, Multispectral, Thermal IR, SAR Radar, Magnetometer Boom) onto a CDS Rev 13 chassis with live hover holograms and snap-in animations.
• 6 Competing Engineering Budgets & Launch Gate: Every part modifies Mass (1.33 kg/U), Sunlight/Eclipse Power, Budget, Onboard Flash, RF Link Margin (dB), and Orbital Lifetime—enforcing realistic mechanical, pointing, launcher, and de-orbit blockers before liftoff.
• Deterministic SGP4 Flight & Live Earth Weather: Powered by satellite.js, a synchronized 3D Earth terminator & 2D curved ground-track map simulate target science passes, thermal/power anomalies, Safe Mode brownouts, and ground-station downlinks (Abuja CSID, Svalbard, Wallops, Singapore). Live Meteomatics API cloud cover and precipitation degrade optical sensors and cause X-band RF rain fade (with an automatic climatological fallback).
• 1–4 Player Collaboration & Education: Supports 4-Player Co-op Crew (Director, Engineer, Science, Comms with cross-role design proposals over WebSockets), Competitive Team Race, a 60-second Guided Tour, a 4-tab Space Systems Field Guide (Beginner & Intermediate), and an AI Flight Director.

Tools, Stack & Factors Considered
Built with TypeScript, React, Three.js / React Three Fiber, Zustand, Express, WebSockets (ws), satellite.js, Tailwind CSS, Web Audio API procedural synthesis, and Vitest (44 automated unit/integration tests). Key design priorities included strict CDS Rev 13 accuracy, mobile browser performance (InstancedMesh, LOD culling, progressive texture hot-swapping), and accessible plain-English learning alongside real orbital math.

Super Intelligence (SI) Acknowledgment
This project integrates the Google Gemini API (@google/genai) server-side to power an optional, state-aware AI Flight Director Coach and Post-Mission Engineering Critique (paired with a deterministic rule-based fallback). AI coding assistance was also used during software development, debugging, and documentation, while all physics, orbital propagation, scoring, 3D geometry, and procedural audio run deterministically.
